newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HINGIS MAKES BIG IMPRESSION ON GRAF, SELES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS MAKES BIG IMPRESSION ON GRAF, SELES.

text.p: Martina Hingis lost her first career Grand Slam semifinal on Saturday, but the Swiss 15-year-old made quite an impression on the current queens of tennis.
Steffi Graf and Monica Seles, who will battle for U.S. Open supremacy on Sunday, share not only the world number one ranking but an admiration for the game of the rising young star.
"The way she has been playing, you can't really look at her as a 15-year-old," said Graf after her exciting 7-5 6-3 victory over Hingis on Saturday.
"She has been playing so well it doesn't seem like you have got somebody really that young across the net.
"I'm sure I wasn't as consistent as she was at that age," added Graf, who won the first of her 20 major titles at the French Open just before turning 18.
The Czechoslovak-born Hingis has almost had greatness forced upon her, being named for tennis legend Martina Navratilova.

By the age of 12, it was becoming clear that she might actually live up to her lofty moniker when she became the youngest French Open junior champion. She repeated that title and won the Wimbledon junior crown the following year.

"She plays very effortlessly. I think it is beautiful to watch Martina play," said Seles. "She is also a very strong competitor. She has amazing poise, amazing mental ability and just a great sense of the court."
Graf agreed that Hingis not only has the shots to make her a champion, but the smarts to go with it.
"She really has both of them," Graf said.

This year Hingis really has come into her own. She became the youngest ever Austrialian Open quarter-finalist, upset Graf in Rome, and displayed incredible poise in taking out 1994 Open champion Arantxa Sanchez Vicario and seventh-ranked Jana Novotna this week.
Hingis also appears to have the temperament of a champion, showing little patience with herself when she makes an error on court, even against a player who forces errors out of the best of them.
"The last few months I think that she realised that she can beat the top players," Graf said of Hingis, who tends to abuse her racket when frustrated with her performance.
"She has beaten me before. Now she has gotten the sense that she can beat everybody," Graf said.
"If she keeps going at this rate," said Seles, "well, she already is unbelievable."
